subject: Michal Šimečka (Progressive Slovakia) and journalist Monika Tódová, apparently discussing rigging the election
called_fake_by: Michal Šimečka and the newspaper Denník N
claim: Two days before the national election, inside the 48-hour pre-election silence period, audio spread in which Šimečka and a well-known journalist seemed to discuss buying votes. Both said right away that it was fake.
finding: AFP fact-checkers reported that the experts they consulted saw signs of AI voice synthesis in the audio. It can't be relied on as a record of any real conversation. How it was made, and from what source material, wasn't established.
outcome: Robert Fico's party beat Šimečka's. Some commentators blamed the clip. Researchers in the Harvard Misinformation Review argue its effect was never shown and point to deeper causes, such as low trust in government and media.
